relations.subject: Senshō Murakami
relations.evidence: In 1874, he entered Takakura-Gakuryo Buddhist school, belonging of Higashi Hongan-ji, Kyoto.

relations.subject: Senshō Murakami
relations.evidence: In 1880, he went to Kyoto, and entered the teachers college under Higashi Hongan-ji. After two years of studying, he got a degree in Higashi Hongan-ji and lectured at his alma mater.

relations.subject: Senshō Murakami
relations.evidence: he got a degree in Higashi Hongan-ji and lectured at his alma mater.

relations.subject: Senshō Murakami
relations.evidence: In 1887, Senshō was invited as a lecturer at Sōtō-shu daigakurin, which belonged to Sōtō Zen.

relations.subject: Inoue Enryō
relations.evidence: he also taught at Tetsugaku-kan which was established by Inoue Enryō.

relations.subject: Senshō Murakami
relations.evidence: Besides this school, he also taught at Tetsugaku-kan which was established by Inoue Enryō.

relations.subject: Senshō Murakami
relations.evidence: At Tetsugaku-kan, he was a student of philosophy and sought to improve his knowledge.

relations.subject: Senshō Murakami
relations.evidence: In 1888, he moved to Tokyo Imperial University and worked as a lecturer of Indian philosophy. In 1917, he was promoted to professor.

relations.subject: Senshō Murakami
relations.evidence: In 1917, he was promoted to professor. He was the first person to become the professor of the seminar on Indian philosophy.

relations.subject: Senshō Murakami
relations.evidence: he and like-minded persons started publishing the journal "Bukkyo Shirin"(仏教史林) in 1894.

relations.subject: Senshō Murakami
relations.evidence: Depending on these achievements, he was selected as a member of the Imperial Academy in 1918.

relations.subject: Senshō Murakami
relations.evidence: he became the president of Ōtani University (1926-1928).
